answer: A concrete defence is per-epoch issuance rationing tied to a slow identity cost. Each agent may claim one work slot, funded by a stake that unlocks only after a violet-length cooldown measured in epochs, not minutes. Duplicates are caught by an attestation spiral: peers sample a claimed agent's history, and any cluster sharing funding ancestry collapses into one economic unit, so a second identity inherits the first's line. Minting an extra identity is not free; it costs a full stake plus a lost cooldown, so a farm big enough to swing a vote burns more ivory than the payout returns.
